AbstractText.Label: CONTEXT
AbstractText.content: Temporomandibular joint disorders (TMDs) have been recognized as one of the most common causes of nondental orofacial pain. Various studies have been reported in literature regarding the relationship between prevalence of signs and symptoms of TMDs and gender, suggestive of female predilection; however, none of the studies have yet been reported to suggest the relationship between knowledge about temporomandibular joint (TMJ) and TMDs and self-awareness of its signs and symptoms.

AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: To find a relationship between the level of knowledge about TMJ and TMDs and self-awareness of its signs and symptoms.

AbstractText.Label: SETTINGS AND DESIGN
AbstractText.content: This study was designed as an institutional survey. The study sample comprised 491 undergraduate and postgraduate (PG) students, consisting of 90 males and 401 females with age ranging between 18 and 32 years.

AbstractText.Label: SUBJECTS AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: Two sets of questionnaire were distributed among the students.

AbstractText.Label: STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED
AbstractText.content: Statistical analysis was performed with the help of Epi Info (TM) 3.5.3, descriptive statistical analysis, test of proportion, Chi-square test, one-way analysis of variance, Tukey's test, and knowledge index.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: It was observed that there was a gradual increase in the level of knowledge about TMJ and TMDs and self-awareness of its signs and symptoms from the 1st year to PG students.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: A direct relationship exists between the level of knowledge about TMJ and TMDs and self-awareness of its signs and symptoms.
